limits: A valid receipt says each party’s key signed its own part and the parts chain. It does not say any party told the truth.

The carried keys are the parties’ only if the verifier already holds those key_ids from somewhere else. A receipt cannot vouch for its own keys. When two roles are signed by one key, one holder signed both.
The acceptance names who accepted. The signature proves the acceptor’s key signed the receipt, not that the person named did.
money none means no money is held or paid by this receipt.
limits is not covered by the signature: someone who removes it leaves a receipt that still verifies.
The checks prove only what they test. A passed record says the pinned commands exited 0 on that tree, not that the work is good.
A test that cannot fail is not detected by this record.

The checker ran them as recorded only as far as the verifier trusts the checker’s key. The signature proves the holder of the carried key issued the record, and content_hash that it was not edited since; the carried key is the checker’s only if the verifier already holds that key_id from somewhere else.
limits is not covered by the signature: someone who removes it leaves a record that still verifies.
A delivery says what the doer’s Tick recorded handing in, not that the work is right. The signature proves the holder of the carried key issued it, and content_hash that it was not edited since.
cents marked reported came from the agent’s platform and were not measured.
It does not prove the order exists or that this delivery answers it; that is checked where a receipt binds the two.
The carried key is the doer’s only if the verifier already holds that key_id from somewhere else. A delivery cannot vouch for its own key.
limits is not covered by the signature: someone who removes it leaves a delivery that still verifies.
A work order says what was asked, not that anything was done. The signature proves the holder of the carried key issued it, and content_hash that it was not edited since.
The carried key is the buyer’s only if the verifier already holds that key_id from somewhere else. A work order cannot vouch for its own key.
limits is not covered by the signature: someone who removes it leaves a work order that still verifies.
payment none means no money is held for this order.

WHAT HAPPENED (2026-10-28). A project started with toward TN (run 01a1828d-2b1d-76c8-8d2a-5f4869cadcfd), whose tasks each named a unit of TN (TN0.38, TN0.39, TN0.41, by tick_send's `unit`), landed all its work, and then its finish step failed: "FINISH_TRACKER_FAILED: finish-provider: the goal tracker (memory settle) could not be told, so the project is not closed: memory__settle: TN is a document ladder, finished by its milestones' units; report toward one of its units." The refusal is planSettle's (packages/api/src/memory-settle.ts, about line 184: `goal.type === 'ladder' && goal.kind !== 'series'`). tick_project start accepts toward TN, and tick_send names units of TN, so a project carrying several units of a document ladder has no goal it can finish toward. The older project "Receipts that prove something to someone else (TN0, the road redrawn, GD-68)", run 01a16851, also toward TN, sits open the same way.

WHAT TO BUILD.
1. A report toward a document ladder settles the units the project carried that belong to that ladder: each such unit, not already done, is amended done with the finish's evidence (as a unit goal is today, the `done` loop near the end of settle), and the finish itself is recorded toward the ladder, linked about it, as a series finish is. The ladder itself is never retired or made done by a project: a document ladder is finished by its milestones. Which units belong to it: the carried unit's record names its milestone (props.milestone, e.g. "TN0"), and the milestone's record (ms:<id>) is part_of ladder:<goal>; read them through the state reader as the other records are.
2. packages/api/src/memory-settle-state.ts readSettleState (about line 360) wants only `asLadder.units` or the goal id; for a document ladder goal it must also load the units the report carries (carriedBy in memory-settle.ts reads report.units), so the planner can amend them.
3. Refused as today, with today's sentence: a report toward a document ladder that carries no unit of it (packages/api/src/memory-settle.test.ts, "refuses a document ladder, and a goal the memory does not hold", about line 185, uses a report that carries none: it must still pass unchanged), and any settle of a document ladder by --observed or --release (packages/api/src/memory-settle-release.test.ts:177 expects "is a document ladder"; keep it).
4. The project is finished once every carried unit of the ladder is done and no other open project works toward it, as for a series; another open project toward the same ladder (run 01a16851 exists) leaves it waiting, and that wait is a wait, not a problem: the finish step closes the project (read how a series finish with `live > 0` is answered, and do the same).
5. Tests in a new file, packages/api/src/memory-settle-document.test.ts, built with the helpers of packages/api/src/memory-settle.test-support.ts: a report toward TN carrying TN0.38 and TN0.39 (milestone TN0, ms:TN0 part_of ladder:TN) makes both done with the finish's evidence and records the finish about ladder:TN; a carried unit of another ladder is left alone; an already-done unit is not amended again; a report carrying none is refused with today's sentence; the ladder is never retired. Keep memory-settle.ts (367 lines) and memory-settle-state.ts (433) under 500. Grep the whole tree's *.test.ts for "document ladder", planSettle and readSettleState before you finish. If another file must change, ask for it with tick_widen; never weaken or delete a test.

DONE WHEN. Tick's check passes on your commit (call tick_check; do not install, build or run suites in your copy).
